neighbours.label: two paired things set against each other: context predicting 'opposite / opposing / anti-' (strands run in opposing directions, same or opposite)
fire: The two currents flow in opposite directions through the parallel wires.
In a double helix the two strands are antiparallel, pointing in opposing directions.
The two gears turn in opposite directions where their teeth meet.
The phase of the reflected wave can be either the same or the opposite.
At a transform boundary two plates slide past each other in opposite directions.
The two forces are equal in size but act in opposite directions.
The north and south poles of the two magnets face each other and attract.
The two signals are perfectly anticorrelated, one rising as the other falls.
quiet: The current flows through the single wire to the lamp on the desk.
In a cell the DNA is packed tightly into chromosomes in the nucleus.
The gear turns slowly when the motor is switched on.
The phase of the wave depends on its frequency and the medium.
At a boundary the rock is often folded and fractured by pressure.
The force is measured in newtons using a spring balance.
The magnet sticks to the fridge door and holds up a postcard.
The signal is strong near the tower and weak in the valley.

notes: Card: heavily anticorrelated, same [or] opposite, two [strands] run in opposing directions, landmass[es] compressed together. + pole output suppresses opposite/cross/oppose. Probe: magnets' poles faced in opposite directions 0.63.
